name: s4-compartmental-energetic-coupling
title: S4 — Compartmental energetic coupling: does internalization pay for itself?
concept: Endosymbiotic dependence made operational as net ATP / biomass benefit under transport losses, upkeep, and host-symbiont conflict. Two intracellular metabolic networks, transporters, membrane potentials, and energetic accounting composed; external association vs intracellular coupling compared.
question: Does internalization increase net fitness given ATP production, transport losses, upkeep, and host-symbiont conflict — and in which parameter regimes is internalization actually harmful?
hypothesis: Internalization is net energy-positive only in a restricted regime: where symbiont ATP export exceeds the host's transport + upkeep + conflict costs. Outside that regime, an externally associated partner (S2) has equal or higher net fitness.
claim: An enclosed partner may develop organelle-like function only under restricted physiological conditions: internalization yields a net ATP/biomass benefit solely where export exceeds transport, upkeep, and conflict costs, bounded by proton-gradient constraints — and there exist regimes where internalization is energetically harmful relative to external association.

behavior_tests.name: internalization-net-energy-positive
behavior_tests.description: Net ATP/biomass benefit of the internalized configuration exceeds the external one.

provenance.note: Net ATP flux (internalized) minus net ATP flux (external association), per biomass; >0 in at least one regime. Enzyme/pathway ancestry priors from Santana-Molina-2025.

behavior_tests.name: harmful-regime-exists
behavior_tests.description: There exists a parameter regime where internalization is net-negative (honest failure route).

literature_anchors.expectation: Central carbon metabolism has chimeric host+partner enzyme ancestry.
literature_anchors.source: Santana-Molina et al. 2025, Nature Ecology & Evolution

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: Composite NOT yet built. Requires: two intracellular metabolic networks (reuse S1 GEMs), explicit transporters + membrane potentials, and an ATP/biomass accounting process; external-vs-internal arms.
